reference_note: EZ-USB FX2LP serial-EEPROM boot formats as documented in the public device datasheet and technical reference manual. Offsets and field meanings are transcribed from public documentation only; no value here is derived from any device dump.
endianness_note: Identifier fields (VID/PID/DID) are stored little-endian (LSB first). C2 firmware data-record length and address words are stored big-endian (MSB first).

boot_formats.C0: Identifier-only image: overrides VID/PID/DID and the configuration byte; no 8051 firmware is loaded from EEPROM.
boot_formats.C2: Firmware image: identifier header followed by one or more code/data records loaded into internal RAM, terminated by a final record that releases the 8051 from reset.

fields.name: boot_config_byte
fields.description: Leading boot-configuration byte that selects the EEPROM boot format (0xC0 identifier-only, 0xC2 firmware load). Any other value means the controller ignores the EEPROM.

fields.name: vid
fields.description: USB Vendor ID override word (LSB at 0x01, MSB at 0x02).

fields.name: pid
fields.description: USB Product ID override word (LSB at 0x03, MSB at 0x04).

fields.name: did
fields.description: USB Device release / Device ID override word (LSB at 0x05, MSB at 0x06).

fields.name: config_byte
fields.description: Configuration byte holding the I2C bus-speed select bit and the disconnect (DISCON) control bit as defined in the public datasheet.

fields.name: data_record_length
fields.description: First C2 firmware data-record length word (MSB first). The high bit of this word on the final record flags the end of the record list.

fields.name: data_record_address
fields.description: First C2 firmware data-record load address word (MSB first): the internal-RAM destination for the following payload bytes.

fields.name: data_record_payload
fields.description: Payload bytes of the first C2 firmware data record. Records repeat (length, address, payload) until the final record is reached.

fields.name: final_record
fields.description: Terminating C2 record: a single payload byte written to the reset-control register at 0xE600 to release the 8051 core from reset once all firmware records are loaded.
